max_area.py.description: After moving left, compares nums[left] to nums[right - 1] instead of nums[left - 1], so a taller left line is skipped. max_area([1, 5, 10, 6]) returns 3 instead of 10.

three_sum.py.description: After finding a triplet, left is not advanced past equal values, so the same triplet is added twice. three_sum([-2, 0, 0, 2, 2], 0) returns [[0, 2, -2], [0, 2, -2]].

palindrome.py.description: When the left pointer meets the right one while skipping non-alphanumeric characters, the function returns False instead of True. is_palindrome('a,,a') and is_palindrome(',,,') return False.
Dead code: the right skip loop always stops on the character the left pointer already found, so this return False can never run. Unreachable for every string up to length 8 over 'a', 'b', ','.

product_except_self.py.description: [] * len(nums) creates empty lists, so the first index assignment raises IndexError. Should be [1] * len(nums).
The skip condition checks i == len(nums), which is never true, so the first iteration reads right_reuslts[len(nums)] and raises IndexError. Should be i == len(nums) - 1.

user_utils.py.description: not (flags ^ flags) is always True, so the second condition does nothing. The function is still correct: it returns bool(flags & 8).

store.py.description: process_payment records raw_subtotal (before discount and tax) as charged_amount instead of total_amount. With 1 Laptop and SUMMER10 the record says 1200.0 instead of 1263.6.
validate_cart checks stock per entry, not per item total. Two entries of item_01 with quantity 6 pass with stock 10; the second deduct_stock then does nothing, so 12 are sold and stock ends at 4.
calculate_total ignores the ENABLE_DISCOUNTS setting. With it set to False, SUMMER10 still gives 1263.6 for 1 Laptop instead of 1404.0.

issues.title: Left-pointer skip check compares against nums[right-1] instead of the old left height
issues.explanation: After `left += 1`, the code should skip the area calculation only if the new line is not taller than the previous left line, which is `nums[left-1]`. This mirrors the right branch, which compares `nums[right]` with `nums[right+1]`. Instead it compares with `nums[right-1]`, an unrelated element. Areas that could be the maximum get skipped.
issues.example: max_area([1, 3, 4, 4]) returns 3, but the correct answer is 6 from the lines at indices 1 and 3.
issues.fix: Use `if nums[left] <= nums[left - 1]:`. Better still, remove the flag and always compute the area.
issues.test_code:
r = max_area([1, 3, 4, 4])
assert r == 6, r

issues.title: Wrong comparison after moving left pointer skips needed area calculations
issues.explanation: After `left += 1`, the code compares the new left height with `nums[right - 1]`. It should compare it with the previous left height, `nums[left - 1]`. The right-pointer branch does this correctly by comparing with `nums[right + 1]`. The wrong comparison sets `calc_area_flag` to False when it shouldn't, so the code skips evaluating valid candidate containers and can return a too-small result. A random comparison against brute force found about 10% of small inputs wrong.
issues.example: max_area([0, 6, 1]) returns 0, but the correct answer is 1. max_area([1, 2, 4, 3]) returns 3, but the correct answer is 4.
issues.fix: Use `if nums[left] <= nums[left - 1]:`. Better, drop the flag and compute the area every iteration, which is still O(n).
issues.test_code:
assert max_area([0, 6, 1]) == 1, max_area([0, 6, 1])
assert max_area([1, 2, 4, 3]) == 4, max_area([1, 2, 4, 3])

issues.title: Unnecessary calc_area_flag optimization adds complexity and hides the bug
issues.explanation: The flag duplicates logic to skip area calculations that are cheap. The two branches are asymmetric, and that asymmetry is where the bug came from. Computing the area every iteration is simpler and cannot be wrong in this way.
issues.fix: Remove the flag and always compute `best = max(best, calc_area(...))`.

issues.title: Left-pointer skip check compares against the wrong element
issues.explanation: After `left += 1`, the code compares `nums[left]` with `nums[right - 1]`. It should compare with the previous left line, `nums[left - 1]`. The wrong comparison sets `calc_area_flag` to False when it shouldn't, so valid candidate containers are skipped. This gives wrong results. For `[0, 3, 5]` the function returns 0, but the answer is 3, from the lines at indices 1 and 2.
issues.fix: Use `if nums[left] <= nums[left - 1]:`. Better, drop the flag and just compute the area on every iteration, since the two-pointer scan is already O(n).
issues.test_code:
assert max_area([0, 3, 5]) == 3, max_area([0, 3, 5])
assert max_area([0, 6, 5]) == 5, max_area([0, 6, 5])

issues.title: Convoluted skip flag adds complexity and hides the bug
issues.explanation: The `calc_area_flag` optimisation only avoids a cheap O(1) area calculation. It makes the loop harder to follow and it introduced the bug above. The if/else that sets a boolean can be written as a single expression.
issues.fix: Remove the flag and compute `best = max(best, calc_area(...))` on every iteration.

issues.title: Duplicate triplets returned because left/right are not advanced past duplicates
issues.explanation: After a match, left and right each move by one. They do not skip over equal values. Duplicate values in the array therefore produce the same triplet more than once. The docstring says the result must not contain the same triplet twice. Only the outer index `i` is de-duplicated.
issues.fix: After recording a match, advance left while nums[left] == nums[left-1] and left < right. Alternatively, store sorted tuples in a set.
issues.test_code:
res = three_sum([-2, 0, 0, 2, 2], 0)
assert len({tuple(sorted(t)) for t in res}) == len(res), res
assert len(res) == 1, res

issues.title: Input list is sorted in place
issues.explanation: The function assumes callers don't mind nums being mutated. This side effect is not documented. Callers' ordering is silently changed.
issues.fix: Use `nums = sorted(nums)` instead of `nums.sort()`.

issues.title: Duplicate triplets returned because left/right duplicates are not skipped after a match
issues.explanation: After a match, left and right each move by one. They do not skip over repeated values. When the array has repeated values at the left or right positions, the same triplet is appended more than once. The docstring says the result must not contain the same triplet twice.
issues.fix: After recording a match, advance left while nums[left] == nums[left-1] (and left < right). Alternatively, keep a set of tuples and deduplicate.
issues.test_code:
res = three_sum([-2, 0, 0, 2, 2], 0)
assert len({tuple(sorted(t)) for t in res}) == len(res), res
assert len(res) == 1, res

issues.title: Input list is sorted in place
issues.explanation: This code assumes the caller doesn't mind nums being mutated. The docstring doesn't mention the side effect.
issues.fix: Use nums = sorted(nums), or document the mutation.

issues.title: Duplicate triplets returned: no skipping of duplicates after a match
issues.explanation: After a match, left and right each move by one position. They do not skip over values equal to the ones just used. Only the outer index `i` is deduplicated. The result can therefore contain the same triplet more than once, which breaks the docstring's requirement that the result must not contain the same triplet twice.
issues.fix: After recording a match, advance `left` while `nums[left] == nums[left-1]` (with `left < right`). Optionally do the same for `right`. Alternatively, collect the triplets in a set of sorted tuples.
issues.test_code:
res = three_sum([-2, 0, 0, 2, 2], 0)
norm = [tuple(sorted(t)) for t in res]
assert len(norm) == len(set(norm)), res
assert len(res) == 1, res

issues.title: Input list is sorted in place
issues.explanation: The function assumes the caller doesn't mind `nums` being mutated. The docstring doesn't mention this side effect.
issues.fix: Use `nums = sorted(nums)`, or document that the input is modified.

issues.title: Returns False when only skippable characters remain between the pointers
issues.explanation: The inner skip loops return False when the pointers meet while skipping non-alphanumeric characters. The docstring says such characters are skipped, and that a string with no letters or digits is a palindrome. The correct result in this case is True. The same mistake is in the right-side loop on line 22. Both loops should stop and let the outer loop finish, not return False.
issues.example: is_palindrome("!!") returns False, and is_palindrome("a!!a") returns False.
issues.fix: Make the skip loops bounded: `while left_index < right_index and not word[left_index].isalnum(): left_index += 1`, and likewise for the right side. Then re-check `left_index < right_index` before comparing, and return True if the pointers have met.
issues.test_code:
assert is_palindrome("!!") is True, is_palindrome("!!")
assert is_palindrome("a!!a") is True, is_palindrome("a!!a")
assert is_palindrome("") is True

issues.title: Returns False when the middle or remaining part has only non-alphanumeric characters
issues.explanation: The skip loops return False when the indices meet while skipping punctuation. That is wrong. Running out of characters to compare means the string is a palindrome. The docstring says a string with no letters or digits is a palindrome, and that punctuation is skipped. The right-hand skip loop at line 21 has the same flaw.
issues.example: is_palindrome("a!!a") returns False. is_palindrome("!!") and is_palindrome("  ") also return False.
issues.fix: Add a bounds check to the skip loops (`while left_index < right_index and not word[left_index].isalnum()`). Do the same for the right index. Then re-check `left_index < right_index` before comparing, and return True when the pointers meet.
issues.test_code:
assert is_palindrome("a!!a") is True, is_palindrome("a!!a")
assert is_palindrome("!!") is True, is_palindrome("!!")
assert is_palindrome("  ") is True, is_palindrome("  ")

issues.title: Returns False when the remaining middle section has no alphanumerics
issues.explanation: While skipping non-alphanumeric characters, the code returns False when the indices meet. Meeting means nothing is left to compare, so the answer should be True. The docstring says a string with no letters or digits is a palindrome. Lines 15-16 and 21-22 both have this problem. The result is wrong for any string whose inner part, or whole content, is only punctuation.
issues.example: is_palindrome("!!") returns False. is_palindrome("a,!,a") also returns False.
issues.fix: Restructure the loops to `while left_index < right_index and not word[left_index].isalnum(): left_index += 1`, and do the same for the right index. After skipping, if `left_index >= right_index`, break and return True. Otherwise compare the characters.
issues.test_code:
assert is_palindrome("!!") is True, is_palindrome("!!")
assert is_palindrome("a,!,a") is True, is_palindrome("a,!,a")
assert is_palindrome(", ,") is True, is_palindrome(", ,")

issues.title: Lists initialised empty, so every index access raises IndexError
issues.explanation: `[] * n` is just `[]`. `left_results`, `right_reuslts` and `results` are all empty lists. The first assignment `left_results[i] = ...` raises IndexError. The function crashes on every valid input. The prefix and suffix lists also need a base value of 1 at the first and last positions, and the code never sets one.
issues.fix: Use `[1] * len(nums)` for the three lists. This gives the prefix and suffix products a base value of 1.
issues.test_code: assert product_except_self([1,2,3,4]) == [24,12,8,6], product_except_self([1,2,3,4])

issues.title: Right pass starts at the last index and reads out of bounds
issues.explanation: The loop starts at i = len(nums)-1 and reads `right_reuslts[i+1]` and `nums[i+1]`, which are out of range. The guard `i == len(nums)` can never be true, because i is at most len-1. The loop should start at len-2.
issues.fix: Iterate `range(len(nums)-2, -1, -1)` and drop the dead guard.
issues.test_code: assert product_except_self([2,3]) == [3,2], product_except_self([2,3])

issues.title: Typo in variable name and extra O(n) arrays
issues.explanation: `right_reuslts` is misspelled. The separate left, right and result arrays are also unnecessary. The code could build the result in place and keep a running suffix product.
issues.fix: Rename it to `right_results`, or use a single result array plus a running suffix product.

issues.title: Lists initialized empty, so indexing raises IndexError
issues.explanation: `[] * n` is `[]`, so `left_results[i] = ...` fails with IndexError. Every valid input crashes. The left and right arrays also need a starting value of 1 at the boundary element, which the code never sets.
issues.fix: Use `[1] * len(nums)` for all three lists.
issues.test_code: assert product_except_self([1,2,3,4]) == [24,12,8,6], product_except_self([1,2,3,4])

issues.title: Right pass starts at last index and reads out of bounds
issues.explanation: The loop begins at i = len(nums)-1 and reads right_reuslts[i+1] and nums[i+1], which is out of range. The guard `i == len(nums)` can never be true. It should skip i == len(nums)-1.
issues.fix: Iterate `range(len(nums)-2, -1, -1)`, with right[-1] = 1 initialized.
issues.test_code: assert product_except_self([2,3]) == [3,2], product_except_self([2,3])

issues.title: Typo in variable name and wasteful extra arrays
issues.explanation: `right_reuslts` is misspelled. Three O(n) arrays are used where the result array alone plus a running right product would be enough.
issues.fix: Rename to `right_results`, or compute the right product in a single running variable.

issues.title: Arrays initialised as empty lists, so indexing raises IndexError
issues.explanation: `[] * n` is always `[]`. The first assignment `left_results[i] = ...` raises IndexError, so the function crashes on every valid input. The prefix and suffix arrays also need a base value of 1 at the start and end positions, and the code never sets one.
issues.fix: Use `[1] * len(nums)` for all three lists. This gives the base value 1 for the first prefix and the last suffix.
issues.test_code: assert product_except_self([1,2,3,4]) == [24,12,8,6], product_except_self([1,2,3,4])

issues.title: Right pass starts at the last index and reads out of bounds
issues.explanation: The loop starts at i = len(nums)-1 and reads `nums[i+1]` and `right_reuslts[i+1]`, which are out of range. The guard `i == len(nums)` can never be true, because i is at most len(nums)-1. The loop should start at len(nums)-2.
issues.fix: Use `for i in range(len(nums)-2, -1, -1)` and remove the dead guard.
issues.test_code: assert product_except_self([2,3]) == [3,2], product_except_self([2,3])

issues.explanation: `right_reuslts` is misspelled. Three separate arrays are used where a single output array plus a running suffix product would do.
issues.fix: Rename it to `right_results`, or use one output array and a running right product.

issues.title: Parameter and variable named `dict` shadow the builtin; helper functions add no value
issues.explanation: `registerInDict` and `getIndex` take a parameter called `dict`, and `two_sum` has a local variable with the same name. All three shadow the builtin type. The two helpers only wrap a single dict operation, and they use camelCase instead of snake_case. This hurts readability. The algorithm itself is correct: it looks up the complement before inserting the current element, so the two indices are always different and i < j. It runs in O(n).
issues.fix: Rename the dict to `seen`. Inline the helpers as `seen[x] = i` and `seen[value]`, or give them snake_case names.

issues.title: Parameter and variable named `dict` shadow the builtin, and the helpers add nothing
issues.explanation: `registerInDict` and `getIndex` use `dict` as a parameter name, and `two_sum` uses it as a local variable. This shadows the builtin type. The two one-line helpers only wrap a dict assignment and a dict lookup, so they make the code harder to read. They also use camelCase, unlike `two_sum`. The function logic is correct. Every pair is found, `i < j` always holds, and an empty list is returned when no pair exists.
issues.fix: Remove the helpers and use a local dict named `seen`, with `seen[x] = i` and `seen[value]`. Return `[seen[value], i]` directly instead of using a `result` variable.

issues.title: Trivial helpers shadow the built-in `dict`
issues.explanation: `registerInDict` and `getIndex` only wrap a single dict operation. Both, and `two_sum` itself, use `dict` as a variable name, which shadows the built-in. The helper names are also camelCase, unlike the snake_case `two_sum`. The algorithm itself is correct. The lookup happens before the current element is registered, so the two indices are always different and i < j. Duplicate values are also handled.
issues.fix: Inline the helpers, using `seen[x] = i` and `seen[value]`. Rename the variable to `seen`.

issues.title: Redundant `not (flags ^ flags)` clause
issues.explanation: `flags ^ flags` is always 0, so `not (flags ^ flags)` is always True. The clause does nothing and suggests a check that isn't there. The `is_valid` variable is also unnecessary. This assumes bit 3 is zero-indexed, so the mask is 8. The docstring doesn't say which indexing it uses.
issues.fix: Use `return bool(flags & (1 << 3))`.

issues.title: Redundant, misleading `not (flags ^ flags)` clause
issues.explanation: `flags ^ flags` is always 0, so `not (flags ^ flags)` is always True. The clause does nothing, and it suggests a validity check that doesn't exist. The function behaves as the docstring says, but the extra clause makes the code harder to read. The docstring also doesn't say whether "bit 3" is zero-indexed. The code assumes it is, so `1 << 3` is the value 8.
issues.fix: Use `return bool(flags & (1 << 3))` and state the bit indexing in the docstring.

issues.title: Redundant `not (flags ^ flags)` clause
issues.explanation: `flags ^ flags` is always 0, so `not (flags ^ flags)` is always True. The result is correct, because it equals `bool(flags & 8)`. The dead clause suggests a check that does nothing and makes readers wonder what was intended. The temporary variable `is_valid` adds nothing either.
issues.fix: Use `return bool(flags & (1 << 3))`.

issues.title: validate_cart checks each entry separately, not the total per item
issues.explanation: The docstring says the same item_id may appear in several entries. It also says stock must cover the total quantity requested for each item. The loop checks each entry against stock on its own. A cart that splits an item across entries can pass validation even though the total exceeds stock. In that case deduct_stock silently skips the second deduction, so the payment succeeds without the stock being removed.
issues.fix: Sum the quantities per item_id first, then check stock against each total.
issues.test_code:
inv=InventoryService();p=PaymentProcessor(SessionManager(),inv)
r=p.validate_cart([{"item_id":"item_01","quantity":6},{"item_id":"item_01","quantity":6}])
assert r is False, r

issues.title: ENABLE_DISCOUNTS setting is ignored
issues.explanation: The docstring says discount codes apply only when ENABLE_DISCOUNTS is on. calculate_total never reads the setting, so discounts are applied even when it is off.
issues.fix: Wrap the discount block in `if ConfigurationRegistry.get("ENABLE_DISCOUNTS", True):`.
issues.test_code:
ConfigurationRegistry.set("ENABLE_DISCOUNTS", False)
try:
    p=PaymentProcessor(SessionManager(),InventoryService())
    t=p.calculate_total([{"item_id":"item_02","quantity":4}],"SUMMER10")
    assert t==117.0, t
finally:
    ConfigurationRegistry.set("ENABLE_DISCOUNTS", True)

issues.title: charged_amount records the raw subtotal, not the amount charged
issues.explanation: The docstring says charged_amount is the amount actually charged, as returned by calculate_total. The code stores raw_subtotal, which has no discount and no tax. The total_amount computed on line 169 is never used. This also makes AuditService.verify_user_totals return wrong sums.
issues.example: Paying for 4 x item_02 with SUMMER10 records 100.0 instead of 105.3
issues.fix: Use "charged_amount": total_amount and remove the raw_subtotal computation.
issues.test_code:
sm=SessionManager();p=PaymentProcessor(sm,InventoryService())
s=sm.create_session("u")
items=[{"item_id":"item_02","quantity":4}]
expected=p.calculate_total(items,"SUMMER10")
assert p.process_payment(s,items,"SUMMER10")
assert p.transaction_history[0]["charged_amount"]==expected, p.transaction_history[0]["charged_amount"]

issues.title: datetime.utcnow() is deprecated
issues.explanation: utcnow() returns naive datetimes and is deprecated since Python 3.12. This is used in several places.
issues.fix: Use datetime.datetime.now(datetime.timezone.utc).isoformat().

issues.title: validate_cart checks stock per entry, not per item_id total
issues.explanation: The docstring says the same item_id may appear in several entries and that stock must cover the total quantity requested for each item. Each entry is checked on its own, so a cart can pass validation while asking for more than is in stock. process_payment then charges the full price, but deduct_stock silently skips the entry that doesn't fit. The customer pays for goods that are never deducted from stock.
issues.fix: Sum quantities per item_id first, then check stock against each total.
issues.test_code:
inv = InventoryService()
pp = PaymentProcessor(SessionManager(), inv)
items = [{'item_id':'item_01','quantity':6},{'item_id':'item_01','quantity':6}]
r = pp.validate_cart(items)
assert r is False, r

issues.title: calculate_total ignores the ENABLE_DISCOUNTS setting
issues.explanation: The docstring says a discount code applies only when ENABLE_DISCOUNTS is on. The code never reads the setting, so discounts are applied even when it is off.
issues.fix: Check ConfigurationRegistry.get('ENABLE_DISCOUNTS', True) before applying a discount code.
issues.test_code:
ConfigurationRegistry.set('ENABLE_DISCOUNTS', False)
try:
    pp = PaymentProcessor(SessionManager(), InventoryService())
    items = [{'item_id':'item_02','quantity':1}]
    a = pp.calculate_total(items, 'SUMMER10')
    b = pp.calculate_total(items)
    assert a == b == 29.25, (a, b)
finally:
    ConfigurationRegistry.set('ENABLE_DISCOUNTS', True)

issues.title: charged_amount records the raw subtotal instead of the amount charged
issues.explanation: The docstring says charged_amount is the amount actually charged, as returned by calculate_total. The code stores raw_subtotal, which has no discount and no tax. The calculated total_amount is never used. AuditService.verify_user_totals therefore returns wrong sums.
issues.example: Paying for 1 Mouse (item_02) with no discount records 25.0, but calculate_total returns 29.25.
issues.fix: Store total_amount as charged_amount and drop the raw_subtotal computation.
issues.test_code:
sm = SessionManager()
inv = InventoryService()
pp = PaymentProcessor(sm, inv)
sid = sm.create_session('u1')
items = [{'item_id':'item_02','quantity':1}]
expected = pp.calculate_total(items, 'VIP20')
assert pp.process_payment(sid, items, 'VIP20')
actual = pp.transaction_history[0]['charged_amount']
assert actual == expected, (actual, expected)
assert AuditService(pp).verify_user_totals('u1') == expected

issues.title: User id relies on built-in hash(), which is not stable or collision-free
issues.explanation: Python randomizes str hashes per process, so ids differ between runs. The docstring only promises stability within one process, so this is not a bug. Two different usernames could collide and silently replace each other. This assumes that never happens.
issues.fix: Use a deterministic id such as a hash of the username (hashlib) or a counter or uuid.

issues.title: datetime.utcnow() is deprecated
issues.explanation: utcnow() is deprecated since Python 3.12 and returns a naive datetime.
issues.fix: Use datetime.datetime.now(datetime.timezone.utc).

issues.title: validate_cart checks each entry separately instead of the total per item
issues.explanation: The docstring says stock must cover the total quantity requested for each item, and the same item_id may appear in several entries. Each entry is checked against stock on its own, so a cart whose entries add up to more than the stock passes. process_payment then calls deduct_stock for each entry. The later deductions silently do nothing, so the customer is charged for items that were never deducted or never in stock.
issues.example: Item item_01 has stock 10. The cart [{'item_id':'item_01','quantity':6},{'item_id':'item_01','quantity':6}] passes validation.
issues.fix: Sum the quantities per item_id first, then check stock against each total.

assert pp.validate_cart(items) is False, pp.validate_cart(items)

issues.title: User id derived from hash() with an unstated no-collision assumption
issues.explanation: Two different usernames could hash to the same id, and the second would then overwrite the first user. The docstring says ids are stable within one process, so this is not a contract violation. The code assumes there are no hash collisions.
issues.fix: Use a counter or uuid, or key the dict on the username directly.

issues.title: datetime.utcnow() is deprecated
issues.explanation: It returns a naive datetime and has been deprecated since Python 3.12.
issues.fix: Use datetime.datetime.now(datetime.timezone.utc).
